The R template [`analysis-r.qmd`](analysis-r.qmd) has the same sections, the
same figure labels and the same output tables, and produces the same numbers
from the same data.

## Setup

```{python}
#| label: setup
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd().parents[1] / "shared" / "python"))

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from labtools import (budget_table, lsb_volts, pivot_channels, read_run,
                      synthetic_banner, timing_summary, u_quantization,
                      validate_meta)

plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.figsize": (7.0, 4.0),
    "axes.grid": True,
    "grid.alpha": 0.3,
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
})

RUNS = {"reference": "data/reference.csv"}
```

```{python}
#| label: load
runs = {name: read_run(path) for name, path in RUNS.items()}
primary = runs["reference"]
```

```{python}
#| label: banner
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(synthetic_banner(primary.meta))
```

## Data quality

```{python}
#| label: quality
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
for name, run in runs.items():
    problems = validate_meta(run.meta)
    stats = run.meta.get("stream_stats", {})
    print(f"\n**{name}** — {stats.get('records', '?')} records; "
          + ("metadata complete" if not problems
             else "metadata problems: " + "; ".join(problems)) + "\n")
```
